passages.en: Previously, when Du Shu returned from [[Zhao|/maps/map-overall?admin=159]], Ruan Wu of [[Chenliu|/maps/map-overall?admin=39]] was likewise recalled from his post as [[Grand Administrator|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]] of [[Qinghe|/maps/map-overall?lat=36.91514604&lng=115.75902922&name=Qinghe]]. Both appeared before the [[Commandant of Justice|/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-ii-221]]. Ruan Wu said to Du Shu, "As I see it, you have the talent and character to follow the Way, yet lack firmness in upholding it; you have the capacity to hold high office, yet your path to advancement is beset with obstacles; and you have the learning to expound past and present, yet lack singleness of purpose. This is what is meant by possessing talent without putting it to use. Now that you have leisure, devote yourself to quiet reflection and set forth a teaching of your own." While at [[Zhangwu|/maps/map-overall?lat=38.56299818&lng=117.17636367&name=Zhangwu]], Du Shu accordingly wrote the Discourse on Fundamentals in eight sections, and another essay entitled Discourse on Arousing the Nature. Both likely sprang from his commitment to self-cultivation. In the fourth year, he died in exile.

annotations.zht: 《杜氏新書》曰：以為人倫之大綱，莫重於君臣；立身之基本，莫大於言行；安上理民，莫精於政法；勝殘去殺，莫善於用兵。夫禮也者，萬物之體也，萬物皆得其體，無有不善，故謂之體論。
annotations.zhs: 《杜氏新书》曰：以为人伦之大纲，莫重于君臣；立身之基本，莫大于言行；安上理民，莫精于政法；胜残去杀，莫善于用兵。夫礼也者，万物之体也，万物皆得其体，无有不善，故谓之体论。

vern.zhs: 《杜氏新书》集中：杜恕认为人伦的大纲，没有比君臣关系更重要的；安身立命的根本，没有比言行更重要的。安定君主、治理百姓，没有比政法更精深的；遏制残暴、消除杀戮，没有比用兵更有效的。礼，是万物的根本准则。万物都遵循了礼这个根本，就不会有不好的地方，所以把这本书命名为《体论》。

annotations.en: The Du Shi Xinshu / New Book of Du Clan states: Du Shu held that of the cardinal bonds of human society, none was weightier than that between ruler and subject; of the foundations of personal conduct, none was greater than speech and action; for securing the ruler and governing the people, nothing surpassed institutions and laws; and for subduing cruelty and putting an end to killing, nothing was better than the art of war. Ritual gives form to all things, and when all things attain their proper form, all are brought to goodness. Hence he called the work the Discourse on Form.

passages.en: In the second year of Ganlu, Yue Xiang of [[Hedong|/maps/map-overall?admin=57]], then over ninety, submitted a memorial recounting Du Ji's lasting achievements. The court was moved and decreed that Du Shu's son Du Yu be enfeoffed as [[Neighbourhood Marquis|/translations/officials#glossary-capital-neighbourhood-neighbourhood-marquis]] of Fengle, with a fief of one hundred households. Du Shu's memorials, proposals, arguments, and rebuttals are all worthy of attention. Those bearing most directly on the great affairs of his age are recorded here.

《魏略》曰：樂詳字文載。少好學，建安初，詳聞[[公車司馬令|/zh-hant/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-i-198]][[南|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=80]]郡謝該善左氏傳，乃從[[南陽|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=85]]步詣該，問疑難諸要，今左氏樂氏問七十二事，詳所撰也。所問旣了而歸鄉里，時杜畿為[[太守|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]]，亦甚好學，署詳[[文學祭酒|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-054]]，使教後進，於是[[河東|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=57]]學業大興。

至黃初中，徵拜博士。于時太學初立，有博士十餘人，學多褊狹，又不熟悉，略不親教，備員而已。惟詳五業並授，其或難教，質而不解，詳無慍色，以杖畫地，牽譬引類，至忘寢食，以是獨擅名於遠近。詳學旣精悉，又善推步三五，別受詔與太史典定律歷。太和中，轉拜[[騎都尉|/zh-hant/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-i-178]]。詳學優能少，故歷三世，竟不出為宰守。至正始中，以年老罷歸於舍，本國宗族歸之，門徒數千人。

vern.zhs:
《魏略》记载：乐详，字文载，年少时就喜爱学习。建安初年，乐详听说公车司马令、南郡人谢该擅长讲解《左氏传》，就从南阳步行前往拜访他，询问诸多疑难要点。如今《左氏乐氏问》中的七十二件事，是乐详所撰写的。当所问的问题都已经弄清楚后，他就回到了家乡。当时杜畿担任太守，也非常好学，任命乐详为文学祭酒，让他教导后辈学生。于是河东的学术事业十分兴盛起来。

到了黄初年间，朝廷征召乐详并任命他为博士。当时太学刚刚设立，有十多位博士，学问大多浅陋狭窄，又不熟悉教学，几乎不亲自授课，只是充数罢了。只有乐详同时教授五经。有的问题很难理解，向他询问也还是不明白，乐详也没有生气的神色，用手杖在地上比划，旁征博引、类比举例，甚至到了废寝忘食的地步，因此他独远近闻名。乐详的学问精深全面，又擅长推算天文历法，朝廷另外下诏让他和太史一起制定历法。太和年间，他转任骑都尉。详学识优秀但能力不足，因此历经三代，最终没有出任地方长官。到正始年间，因为年老退休回家。他本乡的宗族都归附他，门徒有数千人。

The Weilüe / Brief History of Wei states: Yue Xiang, courtesy name Wenzai, was fond of learning from an early age. At the beginning of the Jian'an era, he heard that Xie Gai of [[Nan|/maps/map-overall?admin=80]] Commandery, [[Director of Official Carriages at Sima Gate|/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-i-198]], was well versed in the Zuo Tradition. He therefore travelled on foot from [[Nanyang|/maps/map-overall?admin=85]] to visit him and seek answers to doubts and difficulties. The extant Master Yue's Seventy-Two Questions on the Zuo Tradition was written by Xiang. Once his questions had been resolved, he returned home. At the time, Du Ji was [[Grand Administrator|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]] of [[Hedong|/maps/map-overall?admin=57]]. He too was deeply devoted to learning and appointed Yue Xiang [[Literary Section Libationer|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-054]], entrusting him with the instruction of younger scholars. Thereafter, learning flourished greatly in Hedong. 

During the Huangchu era, Yue Xiang was summoned and appointed an Erudite. The Imperial Academy had only recently been established, with only ten or so Erudites. Most were narrow in their learning and lacked mastery of their subjects. They seldom taught in person and merely filled their posts. Yue Xiang alone taught all five classics. When some pupils proved difficult to teach and still failed to understand after repeated questioning, Yue Xiang showed no anger. Drawing diagrams on the ground with his staff, he used analogies and comparable examples to explain the matter, often forgetting sleep and food. Thus he alone won renown far and wide. Yue Xiang possessed both profound and comprehensive learning and was also skilled in calendrical calculation. By a separate edict, he was ordered to work with the Grand Astrologer in establishing the standard calendar. During the Taihe era, he was transferred to [[Commandant of Cavalry|/translations/officials/ministers#-nine-ministers-i-178]]. Though eminent in scholarship, Xiang lacked administrative abilities. Consequently, through three reigns, he was never sent out to serve as governor or Grand Administrator. During the Zhengshi era, Yue Xiang retired on account of old age and returned home. He was highly esteemed by the clans of his native commandery, and his disciples numbered several thousand.

annotations.zht: 《杜氏新書》曰：恕弟理，字務仲。少而機察精要，畿奇之，故名之曰理。年二十一而卒。弟寬，字務叔。清虛玄靜，敏而好古。以名臣門戶，少長京師，而篤志博學，絕於世務，其意欲探賾索隱，由此顯名，當塗之士多交焉。舉[[孝廉|/zh-hant/translations/officials#glossary-filial-and-incorrupt]]，除郎中。年四十二而卒。經傳之義，多所論駮，皆草創未就，惟刪集禮記及春秋左氏傳解，今存于世。
annotations.zhs: 《杜氏新书》曰：恕弟理，字务仲。少而机察精要，畿奇之，故名之曰理。年二十一而卒。弟宽，字务叔。清虚玄静，敏而好古。以名臣门户，少长京师，而笃志博学，绝于世务，其意欲探赜索隐，由此显名，当涂之士多交焉。举[[孝廉|/zh-hans/translations/officials#glossary-filial-and-incorrupt]]，除郎中。年四十二而卒。经传之义，多所论駮，皆草创未就，惟删集礼记及春秋左氏传解，今存于世。

vern.zhs: 《杜氏新书》记载：杜恕的弟弟杜理，字务仲，年少时就机敏明察、能抓住关键要点，杜畿认为他很奇特，所以给他取名为理。他二十一岁就去世了。另一个弟弟杜宽，字务叔，淡泊宁静，聪明而喜好古代文化事物。因为出身于名臣之家，从小在京城长大，却志向坚定，学识渊博，不参与世俗的事务，只想要探究幽深隐微的道理，因此他名声显著，当权的人大多和他交往。他被推举为孝廉，被任命为郎中，四十二岁时去世。他对于经传的义理，有很多自己的论述和辩驳，但都只是初稿没有完成，只有删集的《礼记》和《春秋左氏传解》，如今流传于世。

annotations.en: The Du Shi Xinshu / New Book of Du Clan states: Du Shu's younger brother Du Li, courtesy name Wuzhong, was keenly perceptive from an early age and had a fine grasp of essentials. Du Ji thought him remarkable and therefore named him Li. He died aged twenty-one. Du Shu's younger brother Kuan, courtesy name Wushu, was pure and detached, profound and tranquil, quick-witted and fond of antiquity. Born into the family of an eminent minister, he grew up in the capital. Yet he devoted himself to broad learning and withdrew entirely from worldly affairs, intent on probing the abstruse and uncovering the hidden. He thereby gained renown, and many men in positions of influence befriended him. He was nominated as a [[Filial and Incorrupt|/translations/officials#glossary-filial-and-incorrupt]] and appointed Gentleman of the Household. He died aged forty-two. Du Kuan produced many critical discussions of the meanings of the Classics and their commentaries, but all remained unfinished drafts. Only his edited compilation of the Record of Rites and his explanations of Zuo's Commentary on the Spring and Autumn Annals survive today.

預字元凱，司馬宣王女壻。王隱晉書稱預智謀淵博，明於理亂，常稱「德者非所以企及，立功立言，所庶幾也」。大觀羣典，謂公羊、穀梁，詭辨之言。又非先儒說左氏未究丘明意，而橫以二傳亂之。乃錯綜微言，著春秋左氏經傳集解，又參考衆家，謂之釋例，又作盟會圖、春秋長歷，備成一家之學，至老乃成。[[尚書郎|/zh-hant/translations/officials/departments#state-affairs-037]]摯虞甚重之，曰：「左丘明本為春秋作傳，而左傳遂自孤行；釋例本為傳設，而所發明何但左傳，故亦孤行。」

预字元凯，司马宣王女壻。王隐晋书称预智谋渊博，明于理乱，常称「德者非所以企及，立功立言，所庶几也」。大观群典，谓公羊、谷梁，诡辨之言。又非先儒说左氏未究丘明意，而横以二传乱之。乃错综微言，著春秋左氏经传集解，又参考众家，谓之释例，又作盟会图、春秋长历，备成一家之学，至老乃成。[[尚书郎|/zh-hans/translations/officials/departments#state-affairs-037]]挚虞甚重之，曰：「左丘明本为春秋作传，而左传遂自孤行；释例本为传设，而所发明何但左传，故亦孤行。」

预有大功名于晋室，位至[[征南大将军|/zh-hans/translations/officials/military#conquering--garrisoning-065]]，[[开府|/zh-hans/translations/officials#glossary-open-office]]，封[[当阳|/zh-hans/maps/map-overall?lat=30.83899565&lng=112.01347539&name=Dangyang]]侯，食邑八千户。子锡，字世嘏，[[尚书左丞|/zh-hans/translations/officials/departments#state-affairs-034]]。

vern.zhs: 杜预字元凯，是司马宣王的女婿。王隐的《晋书》称杜预智谋渊博，明白治乱之道，他常说：“道德方面，不是自己所能达到的，建立功业、著书立说，或许自己还能做到。”杜预广泛阅览各种典籍，认为《公羊传》《谷梁传》是诡辩的言论，也不符合先代儒家的学说。前人对《左传》的注释没有探究到左丘明的本意，还随意用《公羊传》《谷梁传》的内容混淆《左传》，于是杜预梳理《左传》中的精深微妙的言辞，撰写了《春秋左氏经传集解》，又参考了其他各家学说，把它称为《释例》。又创作了《盟会图》《春秋长历》，完备地形成了自成一家的学说，到年老时才完成。尚书郎挚虞非常看重他的这些著作，说：“左丘明本来是为《春秋》作传，而《左传》于是独自流传。《释例》本来是为《左传》而作，但它所阐发的道理，又岂止是《左传》，所以它也能独立流传。”杜预在晋朝立下了很大的功勋和名声，官至征南大将军，开府，被封为当阳侯，食邑八千户。他的儿子杜嘏，担任尚书左丞。

annotations.en:
Du Yu, courtesy name Yuankai, was the son-in-law of Sima Yi. Wang Yin's Book of Jin records that Du Yu possessed profound intelligence and strategic insight, and clearly understood the principles of good government. Du Yu often said, "To establish virtue lies beyond the reach of men like me; but to establish merit and leave words behind are things that ordinary men may accomplish." After surveying the classical canon, he deemed the Gongyang and Guliang traditions as merely specious arguments. He also criticised earlier scholars for failing to grasp Zuo Qiuming's intent and arbitrarily confusing his work with those two traditions. Weaving together the text's subtle meanings, he composed the Collected Explanations of the Classic and Commentary of Master Zuo on the Spring and Autumn Annals. He also consulted the works of many scholars to produce the Explication of Precedents, as well as the Charts of Covenants and Assemblies and the Long Chronology of the Spring and Autumn Annals. Together these formed a complete school of scholarship, but he did not finish them until old age. Zhi Yu, an [[Imperial Secretariat Court Gentleman|/translations/officials/departments#state-affairs-037]], esteemed his works highly, saying: "Zuo Qiuming originally wrote his commentary for the Spring and Autumn Annals, yet the Zuo Commentary came to circulate independently. The Explication of Precedents was originally written for that commentary, but what it illuminates is by no means confined to the Zuo Commentary. It too should therefore circulate independently." 

Du Yu rendered distinguished service to the house of Jin. He rose to become [[Grand General Who Conquers the South|/translations/officials/military#conquering--garrisoning-065]], received the privilege to [[Open Office|/translations/officials#glossary-open-office]], and was enfeoffed as Marquis of [[Dangyang|/maps/map-overall?lat=30.83899565&lng=112.01347539&name=Dangyang]], with a fief of eight thousand households. His son Du Xi, courtesy name Shigu, served as [[Imperial Secretariat Left Assistant|/translations/officials/departments#state-affairs-034]].

source.en: Jin Zhugong Zan / Appraisal of Officials of Jin (Fu Chang)

annotations.zht: 《晉諸公贊》曰：嘏有器局。預從兄武，字世將，亦有才望，為[[黃門郎|/zh-hant/translations/officials/departments#chancellery-003]]，為趙王倫所枉殺。嘏子乂，字弘治。少有令名，為[[丹陽|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?admin=60]][[丞|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-040]]，早卒。阮武者，亦拓落大才也。案阮氏譜：武父諶，字士信，徵辟無所就，造三禮圖傳於世。
annotations.zhs: 《晋诸公赞》曰：嘏有器局。预从兄武，字世将，亦有才望，为[[黄门郎|/zh-hans/translations/officials/departments#chancellery-003]]，为赵王伦所枉杀。嘏子乂，字弘治。少有令名，为[[丹阳|/zh-hans/maps/map-overall?admin=60]][[丞|/zh-hans/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-040]]，早卒。阮武者，亦拓落大才也。案阮氏谱：武父谌，字士信，征辟无所就，造三礼图传于世。

vern.zhs: 《晋诸公赞》记载：杜嘏有度量和才识。杜预的堂兄杜斌，字世将，也很有才能和名望，担任黄门郎，被赵王伦冤枉杀害。杜嘏的儿子杜乂，字洪治，年少时就有好名声，担任丹杨丞，很早就去世了。阮武也是一个豁达洒脱、有大才的人。根据《阮氏谱》记载，阮武的父亲阮谌，字士信，朝廷征召他为官他都没有去赴任，他绘制了《三礼图》，流传于世。

annotations.en: The Jin Zhugong Zan / Appraisal of Officials of Jin states: "Du Gu possessed both ability and breadth of mind." Du Yu's elder cousin Du Wu, courtesy name Shijiang, was likewise talented and highly regarded. He served as [[Gentleman within the Yellow Gates|/translations/officials/departments#chancellery-003]], but was unjustly executed by Sima Lun, Prince of Zhao. Du Gu's son Du Yi, courtesy name Hongzhi, won a fine reputation in his youth. He served as [[Assistant to the Grand Administrator|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-040]] of [[Danyang|/maps/map-overall?admin=60]], but died young. Ruan Wu was also a man of unfettered spirit and great talent. According to the Genealogy of the Ruan Clan, his father Ruan Chen, courtesy name Shixin, declined every summons and offer of office. He compiled the Illustrations of the Three Rites, which circulated throughout the realm.

source.en: Du Shi Xinshu / New Book of Du Clan

annotations.zht: 《杜氏新書》曰：武字文業，闊達博通，淵雅之士。位止[[清河|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?lat=36.91514604&lng=115.75902922&name=Qinghe]][[太守|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]]。武弟炳，字叔文，[[河南尹|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-032]]。精意醫術，撰藥方一部。炳子坦，字弘舒，晉[[太子少傅|/zh-hant/translations/officials/household#eastern-palace-010]]，[[平東將軍|/zh-hant/translations/officials/military#pacifying--subduing-095]]。坦弟柯，字士度。
annotations.zhs: 《杜氏新书》曰：武字文业，阔达博通，渊雅之士。位止[[清河|/zh-hans/maps/map-overall?lat=36.91514604&lng=115.75902922&name=Qinghe]][[太守|/zh-hans/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]]。武弟炳，字叔文，[[河南尹|/zh-hans/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-032]]。精意医术，撰药方一部。炳子坦，字弘舒，晋[[太子少傅|/zh-hans/translations/officials/household#eastern-palace-010]]，[[平东将军|/zh-hans/translations/officials/military#pacifying--subduing-095]]。坦弟柯，字士度。

vern.zhs: 《杜氏新书》。说：阮武字文业，豁达博通，是个渊博高雅的人，官职只做到清河太守。阮武的弟弟阮炳，字叔文，担任河南尹。他专心致力于医术，撰写了一部药方。阮炳的儿子阮坦，字弘舒，是晋朝的太子少傅、平东将军。阮坦的弟弟阮柯，字士度。

annotations.en: The Du Shi Xinshu / New Book of Du Clan states: Ruan Wu, courtesy name Wenye, was broad-minded and widely learned, and a man of profound refinement. He rose no higher than [[Grand Administrator|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-039]] of [[Qinghe|/maps/map-overall?lat=36.91514604&lng=115.75902922&name=Qinghe]]. His younger brother Ruan Bing, courtesy name Shuwen, served as [[Intendant of Henan|/translations/officials/regional#commanderies-032]]. Ruan Bing devoted himself to medicine and compiled a volume of prescriptions. Ruan Bing's son Ruan Tan, courtesy name Hongshu, served under the Jin as [[Junior Tutor of the Crown Prince|/translations/officials/household#eastern-palace-010]] and [[General Who Subdues the East|/translations/officials/military#pacifying--subduing-095]]. Ruan Tan's younger brother Ruan Ke had the courtesy name Shidu.

annotations.zht: 荀綽《兖州記》曰：坦出紹伯父，亡，次兄當襲爵，父愛柯，言名傳之，遂承封。時幼小，不能讓，及長悔恨，遂幅巾而居，後雖出身，未嘗釋也。性純篤閑雅，好禮無違，存心經誥，博學洽聞。選為[[濮陽|/zh-hant/maps/map-overall?lat=35.61104535&lng=114.9728879&name=Puyang]]王[[文學|/zh-hant/translations/officials/regional#states-087]]，遷[[領軍|/zh-hant/translations/officials/military#central-army-001]][[長史|/zh-hant/translations/officials/military#central-army-003]]，喪官。王衍時為[[領軍|/zh-hant/translations/officials/military#central-army-001]]，哭之甚慟。
annotations.zhs: 荀绰《兖州记》曰：坦出绍伯父，亡，次兄当袭爵，父爱柯，言名传之，遂承封。时幼小，不能让，及长悔恨，遂幅巾而居，后虽出身，未尝释也。性纯笃闲雅，好礼无违，存心经诰，博学洽闻。选为[[濮阳|/zh-hans/maps/map-overall?lat=35.61104535&lng=114.9728879&name=Puyang]]王[[文学|/zh-hans/translations/officials/regional#states-087]]，迁[[领军|/zh-hans/translations/officials/military#central-army-001]][[长史|/zh-hans/translations/officials/military#central-army-003]]，丧官。王衍时为[[领军|/zh-hans/translations/officials/military#central-army-001]]，哭之甚恸。

vern.zhs: 荀绰的《兖州记》说：阮坦出继给伯父，父亲去世后，本应继承爵位，父亲喜爱阮柯，说要把爵位传给他，于是阮柯继承了封爵。当时他年纪幼小，不能推让爵位，等到长大后，为此感到悔恨，于是头戴幅巾隐居起来。后来虽然做了官，但一直没有解下幅巾。他生性淳朴笃厚，娴静文雅，喜好礼仪，从无违背之处，潜心钻研经籍诰命，学识渊博，见闻广博，被选任为濮阳王文学，后升任领军长史，在任上去世。王衍当时担任领军，为他的死哭得非常悲痛。

annotations.en: The Records of Yan province (Xun Chuo) states: Ruan Tan had been adopted to continue the line of their paternal uncle. When their uncle died, he should have inherited the title. Their father, however, favoured Ruan Ke and claimed that Ruan Tan had named him as his heir, so Ruan Ke succeeded to the fief. Ruan Tan was too young to object at the time, but deeply regretted it when he came of age. Thereafter, he wore a plain cloth cap and, even after entering official service, never removed it. Sincere, steadfast, serene, and refined by nature, Ruan Tan observed the rites without fail. He devoted himself to the canonical texts and was widely learned and well informed. He was selected as [[Scholar|/translations/officials/regional#states-087]] to the Prince of [[Puyang|/maps/map-overall?lat=35.61104535&lng=114.9728879&name=Puyang]], then promoted to [[Chief Clerk|/translations/officials/military#central-army-003]] to the [[Commander of the Central Army|/translations/officials/military#central-army-001]]. He died in office. Wang Yan, then [[Commander of the Central Army|/translations/officials/military#central-army-001]], wept for him in profound grief.
